summary: Hypocaloric nutrition not exceeding 70% of energy expenditure should be used in the early acute phase.
After day 3 energy delivery can be increased to 80-100% of measured energy expenditure.
Protein equivalents of 1.3 g/kg/day can be delivered progressively during critical illness.
Glucose from PN or carbohydrate from EN should not exceed 5 mg/kg/min.
Intravenous lipid including non-nutritional lipid sources should not exceed 1.5 g/kg/day and should be adapted to tolerance.
ASPEN suggests 12-25 kcal/kg/day during the first 7-10 ICU days.
The 2022 evidence was insufficient for a new protein dose recommendation beyond the 2016 suggestion of 1.2-2.0 g/kg/day.
For adult ICU patients who are candidates for EN either EN or PN is acceptable when similar energy is delivered during the first week.
Routine supplemental PN should not be initiated before ICU day 7 in the population studied.
When oral intake is not possible ESPEN recommends early enteral nutrition within 48 hours rather than delaying enteral nutrition.
ESPEN identifies specific hemodynamic gastrointestinal and respiratory conditions in which enteral nutrition should be delayed or reassessed.
Potassium magnesium and phosphate should be monitored at least daily during the first week.
Refeeding hypophosphatemia is identified by phosphate below 0.65 mmol/L or a fall greater than 0.16 mmol/L and warrants intensified electrolyte monitoring.
When refeeding hypophosphatemia develops energy delivery should be temporarily restricted and then progressively increased under clinical management.
